name: RVIR-CI / RobEnt
full_name: RVIR-CI / RobEnt: BIT remote-controlled vascular interventional robot (catheter and guidewire cooperating on one rail; called RobEnt in the Tiantan clinical papers), with multilevel operation strategy
group: Beijing Institute of Technology (Shuxiang Guo, Nan Xiao) with Kagawa University; clinical partners Beijing Neurosurgical Institute / Beijing Tiantan Hospital (Youxiang Li, Yuhua Jiang, Keyun Liu)
versions: Kagawa remote catheter systems incl. remote angiography on a dog Kagawa-Beijing (chen2023_operating, secondary, ~2012) -> guo2016_design (MR-fluid force-feedback catheter system) -> bao2018_cooperation (RVIR-CI: catheter AND guidewire, 780 mm range) -> yang2019_vascular (fuzzy control, in vivo animal) -> bao2022_multilevel (three force zones, two haptic devices); isomorphic leader yang2022_isomorphic (full: real catheter and guidewire as handles on belt-coupled encoder platforms with linear-force and torque feedback, built after surgeons' feedback from in vivo experiments; Sec. 2-3); in-human operation evaluation bao2018_operation (Biomed. Microdevices 20:34, doi:10.1007/s10544-018-0277-5, title via Crossref, cited as ref. 13 of yang2022). Later BIT-Abrobo reciprocating robot (cao2024_reciprocating) became PANVIS-A: A4 scope, not catalogued here.; string-driven multi-slider slave with an optical-mouse master and kinetics + ADRC control (zhou2022_kinetics; its Sec. 2.2 says the slave was evaluated in bao2018_cooperation); RobEnt, the Tiantan team's name for the robot: first patient (jiang2018_initial, 2018) and ten pigs with micro-devices, a disposable waterproof cover and a sheath sleeve (liu2021_animal, 2021); 2011-15: J. Guo / N. Xiao (Kagawa-BIT) robotic catheter system with real-time force feedback: load cell + fibre-optic sensor (Guo 2011, 2012 ROBIO), Xiao 2012, push-force feedback with a mock-handle leader (Xiao 2015 ICIA) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 6 XI) (belikov2024_evolution; chen2023_operating; li2024_design); 2015: Jia / S. Guo (BIT) interventional surgical robot with force feedback, spur-gear rotation and torque-controlled gripper (Jia 2015 ROBIO; follow-ups Guo 2016, Wang 2018, Guo 2018) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 5 JI) (belikov2024_evolution; chen2023_operating); 2016: Bao / S. Guo guidewire navigation robot with fuzzy-PID force control (Bao 2016 ICMA; Guo 2016 ICMA) (Konda 2025 Table 2 row 13) (konda2025_robotically); 2018-20: Y. Zhao / S. Guo slave with on-line acquisition of the operating force by torque measurement (Zhao 2018 Biomed. Microdevices; 2019; 2020) (Belikov 2024 Fig. 6 ZH1) (belikov2024_evolution; chen2023_operating); 2022-24: C. Lyu / S. Guo robot with a flexible tactile-sensing gripper (FTG; lasso-style grip, force estimated from finger bending; Lyu 2023 RA-L) (Alekseeva 2025 Table 9 row 4, Figs. 10k, 14d) (alekseeva2025_design; li2024_design); 2020: N. Xiao (BIT) balloon-catheter delivery module with two geared conveyor belts on the lab's direct-push catheter/guidewire robot with joystick handles, bench (Yuan 2020 ICMA; host robot and operation logic Wang 2020 ICMA) (Alekseeva 2025 Table 4 row 4, Fig. 13b) (yuan2020_design; wang2020_reciprocating; alekseeva2025_design); 2018: S. Guo / N. Xiao (BIT) real-time master-slave (RTMS) system with closed-loop force feedback and a master handle that measures the surgeon's force (Guo 2018 Biomed. Microdevices 20, doi:10.1007/s10544-018-0278-4; Chen 2023 calls its guidewire mechanism heavy) (guo2018_realtime; chen2023_operating); 2019 and 2022: N. Xiao (BIT) sterile-side drive parts: bevel-gear catheter rotation structure for the guidewire operator (K. Wang 2019 ICMA) and a guidewire rotation-and-delivery transmission that limits slip (M. Cheng 2022 ICMA), both bench-tested for accuracy; Belikov codes the 2022 paper CHEs (wang2019_novel; cheng2022_novel; belikov2024_evolution); 2022-24: Y. Yan / S. Guo (BIT) 3-DoF slave with clamping-bracket grippers (PG2 SEA gripper, TIM 2023), grasping-force passive safety method with Changhai Hospital (TIM 2023) and an SEA haptic leader (ICRA 2024), ex vivo phantom per Alekseeva (Alekseeva 2025 Table 8 row 3, Fig. 10h) (alekseeva2025_design; yan2023_seabased; yan2023_grasping; yan2024_novel); 2022: deep-learning guidewire-compliant control (GCCM) run on the BIT endovascular surgery robot platform, slave rebuilt after Y. Zhao 2020 and Bao 2019, Geomagic Touch X leader, acrylic phantom, five operators: operating force -44.0 %, time -24.6 % (Lyu 2022 Micromachines; Konda 2025 control row 32) (lyu2022_deeplearningbased; konda2025_robotically); 2023: Y. Yan / S. Guo (BIT) spring-based tendon-driven steerable catheter for the group's master-slave robot: 1.5 mm active section (support spring with a 20 mm stainless-steel spine, one tendon, silicone coating) on a PTFE-lined passive section; the tendon pulled by a Maxon motor through a rack and pinion, displacement from the motor encoder; bench only, active section bent against a printed circle grid (radii 22.5 to 6 mm), bending radius from tendon displacement with mean absolute error 0.109 mm (6.53 %) (Yan 2023 ICMA, Secs. II-A, III, Figs. 8-10; Alekseeva 2025 Table 15 row 3) (yan2023_novel; alekseeva2025_design); RobEnt: robot of endovascular treatment with force feedback and cooperating catheter and guidewire (built by Beijing Institute of Technology; clinical team Beijing Neurosurgical Institute / Tiantan Hospital); BIT string-driven vascular intervention surgical robotic system (ADRC control)
target_anatomy: neurovascular: cerebral angiography in a patient (bilateral carotid and vertebral arteries, jiang2018_initial); human body vessel model; pig aortic arch vessels ex vivo
devices_driven: catheter (5 F tested) + guidewire (0.8 mm rod used in rotary test), driven simultaneously by two manipulators on one rail (bao2018 Sec. 4); first patient: 5 F 135-degree angiographic catheter (Cordis) and 0.035-in 150 cm hydrophilic guidewire (Terumo) (jiang2018_initial p. 2); 2021 animals: also Exel-14 microcatheter and 0.014-in micro-guidewire inside the 5 F catheter (liu2021_animal p. 2, 4)
n_dof_detail: 4 (linear + rotary for each of catheter manipulator and guidewire manipulator; bao2018 Table 1)
translation_detail: linear-stage+clamp
rotation_detail: Rotating conical-clamp grasper in each manipulator; assistant grasping mechanisms 1-3 on the rail hold the device while the manipulator returns (bao2018 Figs. 10, 12)
device_range: 5 F catheter; guidewire ~0.8 mm (steel-rod test stand); no stated range limits; RobEnt 2018: travel 0.9 m, linear speed up to 90 cm/s, rotation up to 420 deg/s (jiang2018_initial p. 4); 2021: push 1.2 m, < 5 cm/s, < 180 deg/s (liu2021_animal p. 5)
footprint_mm: rail travel 780 mm (bao2018 Sec. 4.1); overall size N.R.
force_sensing: Proximal axial force per manipulator by strain-gauge sensor behind a low-friction bearing transmission (static connection, to avoid the slip of friction wheels): max relative error 2.53 % (catheter) / 2.48 % (guidewire) vs ATI reference (bao2018 Sec. 5.1). Tip contact: 1.3 mm fibre-optic pressure sensor in a 5 F catheter, 0-0.2 N (guo2019_novel Sec. IV-B).; RobEnt papers: force feedback on the console handle, resistance and vessel contact shown on the console, sensor type N.R. (jiang2018_initial p. 4)
haptics_leader: Bao 2018/2022: two commercial haptic devices (Geomagic Touch X), one per device. Guo 2019: passive magnetorheological-fluid leader around a real 7 F input catheter. Yang 2022: isomorphic leader with real catheter and guidewire as handles. yang2022 detail: catheter and guidewire fixed on their own handle platforms, belt-coupled to encoder motors, with linear-force and torque feedback devices and eccentric force compensation (Sec. 3, Figs. 3-11).; first patient: console with two haptic handles outside the room (jiang2018_initial Fig. 1); zhou2022: optical-mouse master reading axial and circumferential displacement, force feedback N.R.
imaging_compat: X-ray DSA (Siemens Artis zee III in 2018, AXIOM Artis dBA in 2021); robot not connected to the DSA (jiang2018_initial p. 4, 9)
sterility: sterile membrane over the slave, sterilisation time < 1 h (jiang2018_initial p. 4, 6); 2021: disposable sterile waterproof transparent cover and a sleeve at the arterial sheath (liu2021_animal p. 6-7); conical clamp holds the device without damaging its surface (bao2018 Sec. 2.2)
validation_detail: Human: 1 patient (chosen from 5 inpatients with suspected intracranial aneurysm), robot-driven cerebral angiography of both carotid and both vertebral arteries, about 40 min, no complication on 7.0 T MRI at 48 h or at the 7-day follow-up; Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Beijing; local ethics committee approval, no registration stated (jiang2018_initial Secs. 2-4). yang2022 Sec. 2 also cites clinical trials with this robot (Bao et al. 2018, Biomed. Microdevices 20:34, bao2018_operation, not read; patient count N.R.). Animal: 10 Bama miniature pigs (15-20 kg), at least three vessels each (liu2021_animal); pig in vivo trial (yang2019_vascular); dog remote test Kagawa-Beijing via the review chen2023_operating. Phantom: human-body vessel model (bao2018), in vitro model and ex vivo pig aortic arch (bao2022), vascular model 10 of 10 runs to the left subclavian artery (yang2022 Sec. 4.3), 2-D paraffin-wax model (zhou2022 Sec. 4).
key_numbers: CM accuracy 0.11 +/- 0.023 mm and 1.43 +/- 0.30 deg; GM 0.12 +/- 0.024 mm and 1.43 +/- 0.28 deg (bao2018 Table 1); range 780 mm at 20 mm/s; max grip force/torque CM 20.2 N / 24.4 mN.m, GM 18.5 N / 21.6 mN.m; leader-follower mean displacement error 0.038-0.241 mm (bao2022 Sec. V); pig in vivo tracking mean 0.22 mm / 0.17 deg (chen2023_operating, secondary); jiang2018: procedure about 40 min, axial accuracy 0.2 mm, rotation 2 deg; liu2021: mean operation 38.8 min, catheter-guidewire switch 2.8 min, axial 0.1 mm, rotation 5 deg; zhou2022: maximum steady errors 0.45 mm and 6.67 deg with kinetics + ADRC
sim_model: Not of the robot. Kagawa/BIT virtual-reality catheter-operation training simulators model catheter-vessel interaction (guo2012_virtual JRM; wang2016_virtual IJMRCAS, abstract level); no robot-drive simulator found.

name: RAECS / ECRS
full_name: Kagawa/BIT magnetorheological-fluid haptic master-slave catheter system (RAECS / ECRS)

versions: guo2016_design (MR-fluid leader, force-sensor array) -> yin2018_magnetorheological (2-DOF slave, force sensing unit) -> song2018_performance -> guo2019_novel (T-RO: MR leader around a real catheter, fibre-optic tip sensor, collision zones) -> zhang2021_magnetorheological (catheter+guidewire system) -> li2022_collaborative (ECRS: collaborative handles, hydrogel + solid MR fluid, tremor-reduction structure) -> zhang2025_innovative (MRF master interface); 2007: S. Guo (Kagawa) "new catheter operating system" (Guo, Kondo, Wang, Guo, Tamiya 2007, ICME; Rafii-Tari 2014 Table 4 row 2) (rafiitari2014_current); 2014-21: J. Guo / S. Guo grasper-type slave (Belikov GU2.1-2.3): 2014 grasper, 2019 wedge-block guidewire clamp (ICMA), 2020 fuzzy PID, 2021 pinion fixture (ICMA), Liao 2022 (Alekseeva 2025 Table 6 row 5, Fig. 10f) (alekseeva2025_design; belikov2024_evolution; chen2023_operating; li2024_design); 2006: Harbin Engineering University with S. target_anatomy: cerebrovascular / general (endovascular evaluator model)
devices_driven: guo2016: catheter on a slave whose insertion angle adjusts 0-45 deg (guo2016 Sec. 2.4); yin2018 and guo2019: one 5 F patient catheter (7 F input catheter at the leader); zhang2021: catheter or guidewire held by an electromagnetic adaptive collet (Sec. 3, Fig. 4); li2022: 5 Fr catheter and 260 cm J-type guidewire at once, catheter and guidewire manipulation units (CMU, GMU) (Sec. 2.2, 4.4)
n_dof_detail: 2 for the catheter (axial, radial; guo2016, yin2018, guo2019); li2022 CMU + GMU move catheter and guidewire separately (count N.R.)
translation_detail: clamp-relay (guo2019: platform on two stepper motors, grasper A holds for insertion/retraction/rotation while grasper B holds the catheter during A's return; axial grip force 4 N, S8 reading of Sec. II-B)
rotation_detail: Rotation of the holding grasper (radial DOF)
footprint_mm: li2022 slave: 920 mm overall length, 400 mm CMU/GMU travel (Sec. 2.2); earlier versions N.R.
force_sensing: Load cell on the follower for proximal force; 1.3 mm fibre-optic pressure sensor in a 5 F catheter for tip contact force, working range 0-0.2 N (guo2019 Sec. haptics_leader: Passive MR-fluid haptic interface around the real input catheter; resistance up to ~0.5 N at 150 mT (0.4 N at 110 mT); three levels switched at tip forces 0.08, 0.10, 0.12 N (guo2019); ten operators noticed the step at 150 mT in 93 % of trials
imaging_compat: N.R.
validation_detail: In vitro only: guo2016 tracking and force-feedback benches with a vascular model; yin2018 ten novice volunteers drove a 5 Fr catheter through a rigid cerebral model into a wide-neck aneurysm; guo2019 ten operators in the EVE model; zhang2021 ten non-medical subjects in the EVE model with collision cues; li2022 tracking tests and six trialists inserting a guidewire into the EVE model with and without haptics; zhang2025 volunteers reaching targets along a 15 cm vascular-model path (Sec. 4 of each)
key_numbers: guo2019: axial positioning error 1.23 +/- 0.07 mm, rotation 1.57 +/- 0.07 deg; li2022: mean translation tracking error 0.94 mm, rotation 0.89 deg (abstract); MR resistance 0.16-0.5 N across 30-150 mT; guo2016: axial tracking error < 2 mm; zhang2021: axial transmission error < 1 mm (10 runs), 5 Fr catheter driven at 3.5 mm/s in the force test; li2022: CMU/GMU stepping motors 0.36 deg resolution
sim_model: VR catheter-operation simulators from the same group (guo2012_virtual; wang2016_virtual); no physics model of the follower found
